statement: For penalty-aware TSP with carrot constraint (N=200K, 2s), grid-guided 2-opt with penalty-aware exact delta + Or-opt + pos[] tracking + continuous SA outperforms random swap + approximate boundary-only 2-opt by ~9.3 points (78.85 vs 69.5). The critical enabler is grid-based spatial neighbor lookup (O(1), reusing the NN construction grid) which avoids expensive KNN precomputation.
mechanism: Grid-guided 2-opt finds improving segment reversals by looking up spatial neighbors through the same grid used for NN construction. Penalty-aware exact delta computation (iterating over 10th-step positions in the reversed segment) ensures moves respect the penalty structure. Or-opt (single-city relocation with bounded shift) provides additional diversification. The pos[] array enables O(1) lookup of a city's tour position for guiding 2-opt endpoints. Combined, these produce ~9.3 points more than random swap SA because they make spatially-informed, penalty-correct moves.
applicability_bounds: Requires N large enough that random moves are unlikely to find nearby cities. The grid granularity (G=sqrt(N)) balances spatial resolution with cell population.

statement: For penalty-aware TSP under tight time limits (2s, N=200K), grid-guided spatial neighbor selection for 2-opt (using G=sqrt(N) grid, O(1) per lookup) outperforms both precomputed KNN lists (O(N*K) build overhead causes timing variance) and random selection, because it provides spatial guidance without startup cost. Verified: grid-guided scores ~78.85 consistently, KNN-based is timing-sensitive and scores 64.5-78.8 depending on N.
regime: N >= 50000, 2s time limit, grid-NN construction available
mechanism: The grid is already built for NN construction (free). Looking up a city's spatial neighbors is O(1) — select a random cell within radius 2, pick a random city from that cell. KNN precomputation (O(N*K)) takes 0.3-0.5s for N=200K, K=20, which is 15-25% of the time budget and causes high score variance.
applicability_bounds: Grid lookup works well when cities are distributed roughly uniformly. For highly clustered distributions, the grid cells may be very uneven.

statement: Double-bridge perturbation (non-sequential 4-opt) does NOT improve TSP score within a 2-second time limit for N=200K, even with grid-guided 2-opt. ILS with double-bridge (mean 75.7, high variance) underperforms continuous SA without perturbation (mean 78.85, low variance). The O(N) tour recomputation after each perturbation plus shorter SA phases with cold restarts outweighs the benefit of escaping local optima.
mechanism: Double-bridge creates a non-sequential 4-opt perturbation that disrupts the tour structure. For N=200K, rebuilding the tour quality after perturbation requires significant SA time. With only 2s total, ILS manages 2-3 restarts with cold temperature resets, each producing shorter SA phases that can't fully recover. Continuous SA invests all time in a single long anneal, reaching a better final solution.
applicability_bounds: May not apply with longer time budgets (10s+) where ILS has time for more restarts and full recovery after perturbation.

statement: Multi-city Or-opt (segments 1-3) with grid-guided insertion does not measurably improve score beyond single-city Or-opt for penalty-aware TSP at N=200K within 2s. The effect, if present, is below 0.2 points (~0.25% of score).
regime: N >= 50000, 2s time limit, grid-guided SA with Or-opt
mechanism: Single-city Or-opt (relocate one city by small shift) is fast (O(shift) for memmove + O(shift) for pos[] update). Multi-city Or-opt (relocate segments of 2-3) has higher memmove cost and more complex delta computation. For N=200K, the throughput reduction from handling segments outweighs the quality improvement from moving coherent groups.
applicability_bounds: Based on bounded-shift Or-opt (shift <= 15). Unbounded Or-opt was not tested due to throughput concerns.
